title: Analyzing 10,000 Sales Calls With AI In 2 Weeks — Charlie Guo
talk_summary: A single AI engineer analyzed 10,000 sales-call transcripts in two weeks by using a strong model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) with RAG enrichment, chain-of-thought, structured JSON outputs with citations, prompt caching, and extended output limits. The main transferable wins are cost/latency reduction via prompt caching and fewer multi-turn calls via larger output limits, plus the discipline of structured, citation-backed outputs.

takeaways.what_they_do: They reused the same transcript across multiple extraction passes (metadata, insights) and cached the transcript content so repeated calls didn't re-bill/re-process it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: By caching the transcript content, we were able to reduce costs by up to 90% and latency by up to 85%.
takeaways.numbers: up to 90% cost reduction, up to 85% latency reduction

takeaways.technique: Extended output limits to avoid multi-turn splitting
takeaways.what_they_do: They enabled a larger output-context flag so a full summary fit in one pass instead of being split across multiple requests, each of which re-billed input context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Using this flag let us generate complete summaries in single passes rather than having to break the analysis into multiple turns and burning multiple rounds of credits.

takeaways.technique: Structured JSON output with citations to source
takeaways.what_they_do: They forced structured JSON outputs that include citations back to the original transcript, making every extracted claim verifiable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we made sure to get structured JSON outputs where possible in order to generate citations

takeaways.technique: Pay for the strong model when errors are the dominant cost
takeaways.what_they_do: They tested cheaper/smaller models, found unacceptable false positives, and deliberately chose the expensive accurate model because bad output would invalidate the whole project.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They produced an alarming number of false positives... we made the choice to shell out for the more expensive models

takeaways.technique: RAG enrichment plus chain-of-thought before extraction
takeaways.what_they_do: They enriched raw input with retrieved internal/third-party context and used chain-of-thought prompting to improve extraction reliability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We started with the raw transcript data which we then enriched via retrieval augmented generation... chain of thought prompting

takeaways.technique: Turn one-off analysis into a reusable tool/UX
takeaways.what_they_do: They wrapped the pipeline in a simple searchable/exportable tool so other teams reused it instead of re-running ad hoc analyses.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by building a simple yet flexible tool, what could have been a one-off project actually became a companywide resource
